bib.title: Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation with Language Models

question: Can Transformer language models perform multi-step algorithmic computation if trained or prompted to emit intermediate steps into a scratchpad before the final answer?
hypothesis: Single-pass computation limits LMs on algorithmic tasks; letting them emit intermediate tokens gives adaptive compute and improves multi-step accuracy.
contributions: Introduce the scratchpad for Transformers without changing the architecture
Scratchpads help fine-tuned long addition, including OOD generalisation to more digits
Scratchpads help polynomial evaluation in few-shot and fine-tuned regimes
Training on line-by-line program traces with local variables greatly improves predicting execution of Python programs

method.summary: Intermediate algorithm steps are encoded as text in the target between <scratch> tags and the model is trained (or few-shot prompted) to emit them before the answer. Tested on long addition, polynomial evaluation, and Python execution via line-by-line traces with JSON variable states.
method.task: algorithm induction and learning to execute (addition, polynomial evaluation, Python execution prediction)

datasets.name: Integer addition (1-8 digits train)
datasets.size: 100k train examples; 10k in-distribution test; 1k each for 9 and 10 digit OOD
datasets.preprocessing: digits separated by spaces so each digit is one token

datasets.name: Polynomial evaluation
datasets.source: generated, inspired by Saxton et al. 2019; degree<=3, integer coefficients, x in [-10,10], outputs in [-1000,1000]

datasets.name: Synthetic Python programs
datasets.size: 400 train, 100 validation, 200 test programs; 3 random integer inputs each in 0-9

datasets.name: MBPP
datasets.size: 1000 problems, 3 tests each; 374 train tasks (1122 examples); eval split 500 tasks, subset 212 whose traces fit generation window
datasets.preprocessing: discard training examples exceeding context window

datasets.name: MBPP-aug
datasets.source: 80 samples/task from 137B at T=0.5 on the 374 train tasks, outputs recomputed by execution, erroring programs discarded

datasets.name: Project CodeNet traces
datasets.preprocessing: error messages appended to trace then tracing stops

models.name: Pre-trained dense decoder-only Transformers (Austin et al. 2021 models)
models.params: 2M to 137B (addition: 2M-1B; polynomial fine-tune: 8B; few-shot polynomial and Python: 137B)
models.init_from: pre-trained on web documents and dialog data
models.context: 1024 tokens for Python experiments, 512 generation tokens

training.objective: standard likelihood-based supervised training on input plus target (scratchpad plus answer)
training.steps: 5k (addition); 2000 (8B polynomial); to convergence by validation perplexity (synthetic Python); to convergence on MBPP-aug as second stage

other.staged: CodeNet and single-line fine-tuned first, then MBPP-aug
other.lr_scope: learning rate and batch size stated for Python experiments only; addition lr not given

inference.decoding: greedy for Python (T=0); test time by beam search or temperature sampling in general
inference.temperature: 0 (Python); 0.5 when sampling programs for MBPP-aug and synthesis
inference.samples: 80 samples/task at T=0.5 for MBPP-aug generation and synthesis check; single greedy run otherwise
inference.prompting: few-shot: n=4 for polynomial evaluation; 3 trace examples for synthetic Python (Appendix C)

metrics.name: per-task execution accuracy
metrics.definition: task correct only if all 3 input-output examples executed correctly; for tracing the value of output in last trace line must semantically match

metrics.name: per-task trace accuracy
metrics.definition: exact trace match on all examples: every state and the sequence of code lines match ground truth

metrics.name: per-example execution/trace accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of test examples correct across the dataset

baselines: Direct prediction without scratchpad (same fine-tuning or few-shot)
eval.protocol: Single runs; no seeds or significance tests stated. Python eval limited to tasks whose trace fits the 512-token window.

availability.data: single-line dataset by Fraser Greenlee (link not in text)

prompts.where: Appendix C (three worked traces each opened by [BEGIN] and closed by [DONE], then the test function)

evidence.quote: all ﬁne-tuning runs used a batch size of 8192 tokens and a learning rate of 3e-5

results.claim: Fine-tuned addition: beyond a critical model size scratchpad models solve addition while no-scratchpad baselines fail even at the largest scale; the critical size is not stated numerically (only in Fig 3).
results.setup: Pre-trained decoder-only LMs 2M-1B params, fine-tuned on 1-8 digit addition, 100k examples, 5k steps, batch 32
results.quote: beyond a critical model size, models are able to solve the addition task using the scratchpad, while models trained without a scratchpad fail to do so even at the largest tested scale

results.claim: On 9-10 digit out-of-distribution addition, baselines fail completely while scratchpad accuracy rises with model size.
results.setup: As above; 1k test examples per OOD length
results.quote: models trained without scratchpad completely fail, while models trained with scratchpad show consistent improvement as a function of model size

results.claim: Polynomial evaluation, few-shot, scratchpad vs direct.
results.setup: 137B model, 4-shot, 2,000 test polynomials (degree<=3, x in [-10,10], outputs in [-1000,1000])

results.claim: Polynomial evaluation, fine-tuned, scratchpad vs direct.
results.setup: 8B model fine-tuned 2000 steps on 10,000 polynomials; 2,000 test

results.claim: Synthetic Python, few-shot tracing vs direct execution (modified accuracy criterion checks v0 not output; naive scoring is roughly zero).
results.note: Scored on v0 instead of output; 'Under naive scoring, the few-shot tracing accuracy is roughly zero.'

results.claim: Synthetic Python, fine-tuned tracing vs direct execution.
results.setup: 137B fine-tuned to convergence on 400 synthetic programs; 200 test

results.claim: MBPP, very-low-data (374 tasks): scratchpad per-task execution accuracy is below direct execution.
results.setup: 137B fine-tuned on 374 MBPP training tasks; 212 eval tasks whose trace fits in 512 tokens
results.table: Table 3, row per-task execution acc, column Scratchpad MBPP

results.claim: Augmenting with ~17k sampled programs (MBPP-aug) raises scratchpad per-task execution accuracy.
results.setup: As above, fine-tuned on MBPP-aug (80 samples/task at T=0.5, errors discarded)
results.table: Table 3, row per-task execution acc, column Scratchpad MBPP-aug

results.claim: The same augmentation hurts direct execution.
results.table: Table 3, row per-task execution acc, column Direct MBPP-aug

results.claim: Best model (MBPP-aug + CodeNet + single-line) per-task execution accuracy.
results.setup: Fine-tuned first on 9M single-line plus 670,904 CodeNet traces, then on MBPP-aug; 212 tasks
results.table: Table 3, row per-task execution acc, column MBPP-aug+CodeNet+single line

results.claim: Best model perfectly traces about a quarter of tasks (all three examples).
results.quote: nearly a quarter of the tasks (24.6%) are traced perfectly for all three examples
results.table: Table 3, row per-task trace acc, column MBPP-aug+CodeNet+single line

results.claim: Best model exact trace match per example under greedy decoding.
results.table: Table 3, row per-example trace acc, column MBPP-aug+CodeNet+single line

results.claim: Single-line data alone and CodeNet alone each help over MBPP-aug.
results.quote: Training on either the single-line dataset or the CodeNet dataset alone seem to both provide gains over MBPP-aug (23.4% and 25.2% tasks executed correctly, respectively)

results.claim: Tracing fine-tune lowers few-shot synthesis on MBPP.
results.setup: MBPP-aug+CodeNet+single-line model, 80 samples at T=0.5, solved if any passes all 3 tests
results.quote: achieved an overall synthesis accuracy of 54%, compared to the 62% accuracy of the original few-shot model

limits: Scratchpad must fit in the 512-token generation window; MBPP eval restricted to 212 of 500 tasks
Scratchpad is supervised; learning it without supervision (RL) is future work
Few-shot synthetic result uses a relaxed scoring rule (v0 instead of output)
Tracing fine-tune reduces MBPP synthesis from 62% to 54%
Addition critical size is only visible in Fig 3, not stated
No seeds, variance, or optimizer details

terms.definition: an arbitrary sequence of intermediate tokens the model produces before the final answer
